chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: Mama Lou's band with Andrew Jefferson, Al Fonce and Lionel Ferbos
summary: Dawson recalls the Mama Lou's lineup around Andrew Jefferson, a leader with a full briefcase of music, trumpeters Al Fonce and Lionel Ferbos, and where to find them.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Now we had a fellow, who when, most of the time them leaders used to buy so much music, they'd have a briefcase, so full, that it'd have to thin it out, it'd have so much music, some of them old numbers that they wasn't playing, you know, I didn't finish playing for them, it wasn't using them, just clean it out, thin it out, put some new numbers in there. We had, when I was playing at Mama Lou, with Andrew Jefferson, and Raymond Glabion, was playing guitar, Raymond had a briefcase, so full of music, couldn't hardly care, well, he could, he could read good, and, uh, I even thought I'd play trumpet there, he was a good reader, uh, Oh, I was trying to think of his name, uh, He was at the first of the reason the other night, uh, I know we had Andrew Jefferson on the drum, Raymond Glabion, Was this before? And, we had, uh, how do you call him, uh, Morgan, Andrew Morgan, and...
What about, when did you have Herb Moran?
Little Fonce, Al Fonce, call him, uh, Fonce, Al Fonce, little brown-skinned fellow, he worked for the mail service.
What does he play?

Al Fonce, he come up, he come up with, uh, with, uh, with D.D. Al Fonce, Al Fonce, little, little, uh, good, uh, uh, there was two of them that played out there with, uh, with, uh, Andrew Jefferson. This other fellow played trumpet too, he was, uh, he was a good trumpet player, he was over at the Preservation, last week. He lives downtown. I think he works, uh, he's a, he's a, uh, uh, contractor. He works where he's self.
What do you mean, you mean Lionel?
Lionel Favos.
Yeah.
Lionel Favos.
Well, who is Al Fonce?
Al Fonce is a fellow working at the mail, for the mail company.
And he lives downtown?
He lives downtown, a good trumpet player too.
Well, that's funny, I don't know him. I know Herb Moran was there for a while.
Well, he just, uh, Al Fonce played trumpet, just like our, like, uh, Herb Moran. He was good.
I'd like to meet him.
Yeah, well, uh, Favros would tell you where to find him at. You could, you could go to the post office and find Al Fonce.
Well, uh, Norman Kimball ought to know him too, cause he's...
Norman Kimball would know him. You ask Norman Kimball...
And Vernon Gilbert works in the post, huh?
You ask Kimball. He'll tell you who he is.
Is Vernon Gilbert still around?
I know, I know, uh, uh, uh, more than, uh, the banjo player.
No, Vernon Gilbert used to play with John Casimir.
I don't remember. Probably play. You might not know.
